jobs.prompt: tools/machine-limit.mjs already exports memory-aware helpers (readMachine via tools/autotune.mjs, effectiveMachineLimit, memoryPressureHoldLine, jobStartsForBatch, testConcurrencyFor, isNodeTestCommand, applyNodeTestConcurrency, gateVerifyArgvWithMemory) but nothing calls them. Wire them in, small and safe. 1) tools/autopilot-ready-deps.mjs: in autopilotStartReadySettings cap maxJobs by the memory-aware limit (read the machine with readMachine, keep the config ceiling); in startScope, before spawning `go --scope`, re-read the machine and, at hard pressure, do not spawn: return { ok: true, result: 'held-memory' } with one log line from memoryPressureHoldLine; at soft pressure lower --max-jobs by the memory cap. Do not change the shape of the other return values. If tools/autopilot.mjs needs to treat result 'held-memory' like a normal skip (no failure count, retried next pass), do that. 2) tools/swarm/core-31.mjs runChecks: before a check named tests runs its argv, if the argv is a node --test command (isNodeTestCommand) replace or add --test-concurrency=N with N from testConcurrencyFor(await readMachine()); never touch other commands; at hard pressure wait up to 5 minutes (poll every 15 seconds, injectable sleep and machine reader) for pressure to drop to soft before starting, then run anyway at concurrency 1 and record a warning 'ran under memory pressure' in the result. Keep the injection optional through an options field so existing tests and callers keep working with no new arguments. 3) tests/memory-wiring.test.mjs: autopilot hold at hard (spawn never called), soft shrinks --max-jobs, runChecks rewrites --test-concurrency for node --test and leaves other commands alone, waits then runs at 1 when pressure stays hard (fake sleep and machine). No real machine reads or sleeps. 4) docs/memory-limits.md: a short page: the thresholds, the config keys, what is held and why. Keep every existing test passing.
